Compare pairs, method by method

Popular claims often compare two words. Each pair below is recounted from the text under several methods. Where a number matches under one method only, the card says so. Where it matches under none, it says that too.

The number 19, checked

The number 19 is often linked to the opening phrase of the Qur'an. Each claim below is recomputed from the text. Some hold, some do not, and the panel on the right shows how much chance alone would explain.

Claim register and method records

Every claim has an ID, a stated figure, the methods tested, a status and an evidence level. “Reproduce” runs the saved method again against the dataset and checks that the number is unchanged. Changing a rule creates a new version; the earlier one is kept. Each word is counted once, under its main segment.

Your searches

Evidence levels

ADirectly verifiableA count or text fact anyone can reproduce with the same data and rules.
BStrong correspondenceMeasurable, and supported by textual and outside evidence.
CPlausible interpretationDepends on linguistic, historical or method choices.
DSpeculativeA proposed pattern that needs further research.
EUnsupportedNot reproducible, or the method is insufficient.

Letter frequency

Counted from the Arabic letters of the text. Vowel marks, tatweel and Qur'anic annotation signs are excluded, and alif forms (ٱ أ إ آ) are merged into ا. These rules are saved with every result.

Browse the text

Any surah, with word and letter counts for each ayah. Every ayah opens in the reader.

How new themes are added

The first milestone is mathematical. The same framework carries the later themes, so each one reuses the counting rules, records and checks instead of starting over.

1

Define the claim

Write the claim, the Arabic text or words involved, and the counting method before looking at results.

2

Run it in the engine

The engine counts it under every relevant method and keeps all results, including the ones that disagree.

3

Record and review

The method, dataset fingerprint and output are saved. A reviewer reproduces the result before it is published.

4

Publish beside the text

The finished page links each verse to the reader, so readers can check every reference themselves.

Planned themes

  • Ring composition examples
  • Selected scientific correspondences, each with sources and alternative readings
  • Linguistic and rhetorical devices
  • Verified records of past events
  • Textual predictions and what later happened

Every verse links back

Each reference opens the same ayah in the reader, so a number can be checked against the text people already read there.

Built to sit inside the site

Pages can be added to the reader's navigation or embedded as a section of an existing page, in the same calm, minimal style.

Source-first

Numbers come from the Arabic text and its word analysis, never from a translation, and every figure states how it was counted.
